meta.tier: qualitative (what you see) plus line positions for the spectroscope
notes: colorGroup names come from the UBD fact sheet 'Flame colors (chloride salts)'. swatch hex values, brightness words and the masking rule are AUTHOR-SET display choices, not measurements; each is marked author_set.

Line wavelengths and relative intensities come from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database handbook tables (air wavelengths, nm). The NIST intensities are spectral-line-table values, NOT flame brightness. The spectroscope picture may use them only to rank lines within one metal.
Wide bands (Sr 600-700 nm, Cu 500-550 nm) come from physicsopenlab.org 'Flame Test' (author's own spectrometer for Sr; NIST linked for Cu). Draw them as a faint glow behind the lines.
Ca: a real flame also shows molecular emission not sourced here. Mark Ca as needs_review before it ships.
